final_query:
MATCH (p:Person)-[:PERFORMS_VISIT]->(v:Visit)-[:LOCATED_AT]->(:Place)-[:PART_OF]->(:Region)-[:PART_OF]->(:Country)-[:PART_OF]->(c:Continent)
WITH c, p, v, duration.inSeconds(v.duration) AS seconds
WHERE seconds > 3600
WITH c.name AS continent, count(v) AS totalVisits, count(DISTINCT p) AS persons, avg(seconds) AS avgVisitDuration
RETURN continent, toFloat(totalVisits) / persons AS avgVisitsPerPerson, avgVisitDuration
ORDER BY continent

critique.feedback: Everything structural is fine — the chain (Person)-[:PERFORMS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:LOCATED_AT]->(:Place)-[:PART_OF]->(:Region)-[:PART_OF]->(:Country)-[:PART_OF]->(c:Continent) matches the schema's relationship signatures, Continent.name is the right property, and count(v)/count(DISTINCT p) gives the correct 'visits per person' grain (each Visit is LOCATED_AT a single Place, so no visit duplication across continents). The problem is unit/type handling on Visit.duration, which the schema declares as DURATION: comparing it to the integer 3600 (WHERE v.duration > 3600) compares a temporal duration against a number, which is not a valid ordering comparison in Cypher (yields null), so the >1 hour filter would not select the intended visits. Additionally, avg(v.duration) returns a DURATION value, not the requested number of seconds. Derive a numeric seconds value from the duration property first — e.g. bind seconds = duration.inSeconds(v.duration) (or an equivalent whole-seconds extraction supported by your Neo4j version) — then filter on seconds > 3600 and aggregate with avg(seconds) so both the >3600s predicate and the reported average visit duration are numeric seconds.

question: Considering only visits with a duration greater than 1 hour (3600 seconds), for each continent, calculate the average number of visits per person and the average duration of those visits in seconds. Return the continent name, average visits per person, and average visit duration.
